ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Commercial Act of the Republic of Korea, Act No. 19090, as amended; Act on Reporting and Using Specified Financial Transaction Information, Act No. 19264, as amended; Act on the Prevention of Money Laundering and Terrorist Financing and the Prohibition of Financing the Proliferation of Weapons of Mass Destruction; Real Name Financial Transactions and Guarantee of Confidentiality Act; Foreign Investment Promotion Act and its Enforcement Decree; KoFIU Examination Regulations and FATF Recommendations.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Incorporation (Certificate of Company Registration)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Court Registration Office, Supreme Court of Korea (i-register)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille route: notarize the copy at the local notary public, obtain an Apostille from the designated Competent Authority in the state of issue, then prepare a certified Korean translation. Consular Legalization route: notarize the copy at the local notary public, authenticate it at the state Ministry of Foreign Affairs, then legalize it at the Consular Section of the Embassy of the Republic of Korea. The two routes are mutually exclusive alternatives and are never applied in sequence.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Good Standing (equivalent Certificate of Corporate Registration Details)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: National Tax Service and Court Registration Office of the Republic of Korea
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille route: notarize the registered extract, obtain an Apostille from the issuing state's Competent Authority, and append a certified Korean translation. Consular Legalization route: notarize the extract, authenticate at the state Ministry of Foreign Affairs, then legalize at the Korean Embassy or Consulate. Apostille and consular legalization are parallel alternatives; do not chain them.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Board Resolution or Power of Attorney authorizing the Korean incorporation filing
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Board of Directors or shareholders of the ultimate parent/holding company
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille route: sign before a local notary public, attach an Apostille from the relevant Competent Authority, and add a certified Korean translation. Consular Legalization route: notarize, authenticate at the Ministry of Foreign Affairs, then legalize at the Korean Consulate; either route is sufficient and they are never combined.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Articles of Association (or equivalent constitutional document)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Founding members or legal representative of the proposed Korean Yuhan Hoesa
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille route: notarize the signatures, obtain an Apostille from the Competent Authority, and attach certified Korean translation. Consular Legalization route: notarize, Ministry of Foreign Affairs authentication, then Korean Consular legalization. Use only the route required by the country of notarization; never stack apostille after consular legalization or vice versa.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Account-holding bank of the foreign investor or UBO
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille route: the bank's authorized signatory signature is notarized, the document is apostilled, and a certified Korean translation is appended. Consular Legalization route: notarize the bank's signature, authenticate at the Ministry of Foreign Affairs, then legalize at the Korean Embassy; original letters with wet signatures are required, and electronic PDFs are insufficient.

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Every natural person who directly or indirectly owns 25 percent or more of the capital or voting rights, or who exercises de facto control, and each legal representative and director, must be screened continuously against the OFAC Specialty Designated Nationals and Blocked Persons List, the UN Security Council Consolidated List, the European Union consolidated financial sanctions list, the United Kingdom consolidated list, and the Republic of Korea consolidated financial sanctions list administered by the Korean Financial Intelligence Unit and the Ministry of Foreign Affairs. PEPs must be screened against international PEP databases such as World-Check or Dow Jones, and enhanced due diligence is mandatory for any PEP, high-risk jurisdiction, family member or close associate, or adverse media hit; all positive matches must be escalated to the AML Compliance Officer before CDD can be cleared.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Supreme Court of Korea Internet Registration Office (i-register, www.iros.go.kr) and National Tax Service Business Registration System
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The statutory company name must be in Hangul, the Korean alphabet; an English trade name may be used commercially but does not replace the Korean registered name. Foreign-language names must be transliterated into Hangul in accordance with the National Institute of Korean Language transcription and romanization rules. The four-tier naming convention is: (1) a distinctive identifying root or brand name in Korean, (2) the objective or business purpose, (3) the head-office administrative district, and (4) the legal form indicator Yuhan Hoesa or LLC. The name must not be identical or confusingly similar to any existing registered name in Korea.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: Development (when implying a public authority role)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Upon a name rejection, the applicant must first obtain the written statement of grounds from the court registration officer. Within 14 days of the rejection notice, the applicant may file a written correction and re-registration application with the same registration office, attaching a fresh search certificate from i-register showing no identical or confusingly similar trade name. If the rejection rests on a prohibited token, obtain the relevant ministerial license, exemption, or non-objection letter before resubmission. If the registration officer maintains the refusal, the applicant may file an administrative appeal with the competent District Court under the Non-Contentious Litigation Procedure Act within 30 days, and, if necessary, administrative litigation under the Administrative Litigation Act within 90 days of the final refusal.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: For an ISIC 4721 Asian supermarket and specialty grocery retail operation, a virtual office or commercial mailbox is not permissible and will be rejected by the National Tax Service, the municipal Gu office, and Korean banks. The business registration address must correspond to a physical sales floor with fixed fixtures, cold storage, hygiene facilities, and product display areas; the Food Sanitation Act requires the food retail license to identify the actual store. A virtual address is treated as a KYC red flag, may invalidate the business registration, and will prevent the opening of a corporate bank account or merchant acquiring facility for POS and credit card rails.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Initial physical inspection probability: 90 percent because the municipal Gu office and the Ministry of Food and Drug Safety inspector must inspect the store before issuing the food retail license. Annual hygiene inspection probability after licensing: 25 to 35 percent. VAT and tax field inspection probability: 15 percent per year. Physical bank KYC inspection probability: 100 percent for merchant POS and remote deposit capture approval. Checklist: registered business certificate posted at the sales floor, sanitation and personal health licenses, temperature records for imported fresh vegetables and condiments, import declaration and quarantine certificates for overseas food, storage shelf conditions, and the POS terminal or sales data system.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Name clearance search and trade name availability report through i-register and National Tax Service records
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Market benchmark for corporate legal search and written availability opinion; no official court fee for the online search.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: District Court registration fee for incorporation of Yuhan Hoesa
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Court Registration Office of the Republic of Korea
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Court user fee schedule under the Commercial Registration Act, calculated by stated capital and number of registered items; approximate statutory range of KRW 40,000 to KRW 160,000, plus education surcharge.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Notarization of Articles of Association and corporate signatures
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Notary Public Fee Act statutory tariff per instrument and per signature page; market benchmark ranges from KRW 50,000 to KRW 200,000.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Apostille or consular legalization of the mandatory documentary bundle
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Apostille competent authority, Ministry of Foreign Affairs, or Korean Embassy/Consulate as applicable
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Official fee schedule for apostille and consular legalization plus courier and consular processing charges; market benchmark for five instruments.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Certified Korean translation of foreign corporate documents and bank reference letter
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Per-page certified translation market rate and translator's statutory liability endorsement fee; benchmark range of KRW 30,000 to KRW 80,000 per document.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Municipal food retail business license application fee
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Municipal Gu office having jurisdiction over the registered store address
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Municipal ordinance license fee; approximate statutory fee of KRW 15,000 to KRW 20,000.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: AML/CFT UBO, PEP, and sanctions screening and compliance file preparation
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: External law firm and licensed compliance vendor
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Fixed-fee enhanced due diligence package covering UBO piercing, PEP and sanctions checks, beneficial ownership schedule, and risk assessment under the AML/CFT Act and KoFIU guidance.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Business registration certificate issuance at the local tax office
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: National Tax Service, competent tax office
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: No official government fee is imposed for issuance of the business registration certificate.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Commercial Act of the Republic of Korea, as amended, Articles 172 and 287-2 through 287-74 (Yuhan Hoesa LLC), together with the Foreign Investment Promotion Act Articles 5-7, Value-Added Tax Act Article 8, and the applicable District Court registration procedures under the Court Organization Act.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Supreme Court Registry Office, through the Company Registration Division of the District Court having territorial jurisdiction over the registered office (e.g., Seoul Central District Court Registration Division).
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Application for Registration of Formation of a Yuhan Hoesa (LLC), together with notarized Articles of Incorporation and supporting subscription and capital payment certificates.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: None under the Commercial Act: no statutory minimum paid-in capital is required to form a Yuhan Hoesa LLC. However, if foreign investment benefits are sought under the Foreign Investment Promotion Act, a qualified foreign investor must remit at least KRW 100,000,000 (approx. USD 75,000) into a designated foreign exchange bank capital deposit account before registration. The paid-in capital must be actually deposited and blocked in the company's capital deposit account until the commercial registry entry is complete; the bank's certificate of deposit must accompany the registration filing.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLUTION NO. 2025/001 OF THE FOUNDERS, SOLE MEMBER, AND FIRST BOARD OF DIRECTORS OF YUHANG HOESA (LLC), A LIMITED LIABILITY COMPANY IN FORMATION UNDER THE COMMERCIAL ACT OF THE REPUBLIC OF KOREA. The board, having been lawfully convened at the principal place of business and having the requisite quorum of all authorized directors present, adopts the following resolutions, each effective on completion of filing of the application for registration of formation: 1. SHARE CAPITAL SUBSCRIPTION. The Board resolves that the issued capital of the Company shall be divided into ordinary shares of no-par value, that the subscription schedule submitted to this meeting is ratified, and that each subscriber shall pay the amount subscribed for in cash into the Company's capital deposit account at a designated bank before registration. The Board confirms that no share shall be allotted unless the full contribution therefor has been actually received and evidenced by a bank certificate of deposit. The Board authorizes the preparation and maintenance of the shareholder register, execution of share subscription forms, and issuance of share certificates. 2. BANKING AUTHORIZATION. The Board resolves to open and maintain operating account numbers with a commercial bank authorized to conduct banking business in the Republic of Korea. The Board appoints the Representative Director and the deputy signatory named in the minutes as mandatory joint signatories for all withdrawals, wire transfers, and negotiable instruments exceeding USD 50,000. Bank account authorities, treasury management policies, and payment workflow limits are delegated to the designated Compliance Officer. 3. REGISTERED OFFICE ADOPTION. The Board adopts the premises located at the registered office address stated in the Articles of Incorporation as the legal seat, registered office, and principal place of business of the Company, and directs the Representative Director to obtain written landlord consent, to post the statutory signs if required, and to file the location notice with the District Court Registration Division. 4. STATUTORY OFFICER APPOINTMENTS. The Board appoints the following officers for the first statutory term: [Name] as Representative Director and Chief Executive Officer, [Name] as Director and Chief Financial Officer, and [Name] as Compliance Officer and Licensed Responsible Food Hygiene Manager. Each officer is directed to execute all filings with the National Tax Service, the local tax office, the District Court Registration Division, the Municipality, and the Ministry of Food and Drug Safety, and may engage local counsel or certified public accountants for this purpose. 5. GOVERNANCE AND DELEGATION. The Board authorizes the officers and counsel to take all required actions to perfect formation, obtain the business registration certificate, open bank accounts, procure seal certificates, apply for municipal licenses, enter into operating leases, and otherwise carry out the commercial purpose of the Company. This resolution is effective immediately and shall be entered in the minute book and filed with all relevant authorities.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Pre-Formation Name Clearance and Foreign Investment Compliance (if Applicable)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Seoul Central District Court Registration Division; Korea Trade-Investment Promotion Agency (KOTRA) Invest Korea Center for foreign investment notification
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit a corporate name search request on the electronic court registration system to ensure the exact proposed name 'Yuhan Hoesa' is not identical or confusingly similar to any existing company in the same jurisdiction. For a non-resident investor, file the foreign investment notification with KOTRA or a designated foreign-exchange bank before remittance, indicating the business scope (grocery retailing of Asian foods and imported condiments) and the investment amount. Retain the acknowledgment receipt and assign a dossier index number. If the name conflicts with an existing registered entity, cure the defect by filing an amended name or an alternative English transliteration, then proceed to the capital escrow step.
required_dossiers: Corporate name search receipt or pending name registration confirmation
Passport or foreign corporate certificate of the investor
Certified power of attorney
Foreign investment notification form (if applicable)
Business plan and ISIC business code description
Lease contract or landlord consent letter for the proposed registered office
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Submit a corrected name reservation through the same court portal; if KOTRA returns a query, respond within ten Korean working days with amended ownership and business descriptions; if the court portal suspends the filing, obtain the written rejection reason and re-file a revised name application with supporting lease evidence.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Capital Escrow Deposit and Certificate of Paid-In Capital
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Designated foreign exchange bank or authorized domestic commercial bank under the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act; KOTRA for foreign investment certificate registration
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Open a temporary corporate capital deposit account in the exact legal name of the Yuhan Hoesa LLC, deposit the subscribed capital in Korean won from the subscriber's foreign or domestic account, and obtain a certificate of paid-in capital from the bank. The amount and currency must match the Articles of Incorporation and the foreign investment notification. For qualified foreign investment, the remittance must originate directly from the foreign investor's account and must remain blocked until the court registration certificate is issued. The bank will issue a foreign exchange purchase certificate, a capital deposit receipt, and a final balance certificate for use in the registration filing.
required_dossiers: Foreign investment notification receipt (if applicable)
Application to open the corporate capital deposit account
Remittance advice or wire confirmation
Identity documents of each subscriber
AML and source-of-wealth declaration
Final draft of the Articles of Incorporation
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank queries the source of funds, furnish bank statements, investor history, and AML declarations; if the subscription amount is deficient, wire the shortfall within fourteen days and obtain a revised deposit certificate; if KOTRA delays its investment certification, request a provisional acknowledgment letter to continue the court filing.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Notarization and Registration with the District Court Registry
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Notary Public (Korean legal notary office) and Supreme Court Registry Office through the Company Registration Division of the local District Court
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the fully executed and notarized Articles of Incorporation together with the capital payment certificate, shareholder subscription register, founder meeting minutes, board resolution, power of attorney, and lease evidence to the competent District Court Registration Division. The registering judge will verify that the corporate name is permissible, the business purpose is lawful, capital has been paid, and the registered office is physically located within the court's territorial jurisdiction. Upon payment of registration tax, local education tax, and court fees, the court enters the Yuhan Hoesa into the commercial register and issues the corporate registration certificate, corporate seal certificate, and certificate of incorporation. Legal personality is constituted by this registration under Article 287-33.
required_dossiers: Notarized Articles of Incorporation (original)
Bank certificate of paid-in capital
Share subscription forms and shareholder register
Minutes of the founders' meeting and first board resolution
Certified power of attorney for the local filing agent
Lease contract or written landlord consent
Passports and ARC copies of directors and authorized signatories
Seal certificate application form
Registration tax and court fee receipts
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the registry issues a supplementary order or correction request, counsel must respond within the court's stated period, normally seven days, by filing amended pages or additional evidence; if the court refuses registration due to statutory incompatibility, file a formal objection and appeal to the appellate court, or restart the process with corrected articles and a new notarization.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Business Registration and Value-Added Tax Establishment with the National Tax Service
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: National Tax Service, via the local District Tax Office with territorial jurisdiction over the registered office
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Within twenty days after the corporate registration certificate is issued, file an Application for Business Registration with the local District Tax Office. Present the commercial registration certificate, corporate seal certificate, and lease documents to verify the physical place of business. The tax examiner will enter the entity into the national taxpayer database, classify it as a value-added taxpayer carrying on retail trade, and issue a Business Registration Certificate. The same filing activates corporate income tax, VAT, withholding tax, and e-invoice registration. The company may request a bar-coded tax invoice, confirm whether it is required to issue electronic tax invoices, and set up the payroll and social insurance accounts if employees are hired.
required_dossiers: Commercial registration certificate (original)
Corporate seal certificate and actual corporate seal
Lease contract or occupancy certificate
Application for Business Registration (Form 10)
Representative director's identification
Bank account opening certificate
Power of attorney if filed by a certified public accountant
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the tax office imposes a field inspection, provide the requested lease, premises occupancy, and inventory documentation; if the office issues an administrative order to supplement documents, complete the correction within ten business days using the National Tax Service online system; if the business registration is cancelled or suspended, re-file with a written explanation and supporting evidence.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Post-Incorporation Food Retail Report, Fire Safety Approval, and Premises Use Clearance
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: District Gu Office Health and Sanitation Division; Ministry of Food and Drug Safety; local Fire Station of the National Fire Agency; Ministry of Employment and Labor
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit a Food Sales Business Report application to the local Gu Office at least twenty days before the planned opening of the grocery store. The public health inspector will review the facility layout, refrigerated display cases, cold-chain temperature logs, imported food labeling compliance, storage cleanliness, and vermin controls. Concurrently file a fire safety inspection application with the local fire station, which will verify fire extinguishers, emergency exits, evacuation routes, and any required automatic fire suppression system. If the building has recently been built or altered, obtain the Certificate of Completion for Fire-Fighting Systems and the municipal structural occupancy approval. If five or more workers are engaged, register the workplace occupational safety plan and appoint a safety and hygiene manager.
required_dossiers: Food Sales Business Report application and health questionnaire
Business Registration Certificate copy
Lease contract and floor plan
Facility layout and cold-chain equipment specifications
Certificate of licensed food hygiene manager
Fire-fighting systems completion certificate
Certificate of fire safety inspection
Waste disposal contract with licensed hauler
Imported food label compliance declarations for foreign groceries
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Gu Office issues a deficiency letter for facility layout or labeling, correct the deficiency within seven business days and resubmit photos and floor plans; if the fire station issues a serious defect order, engage a licensed fire protection installer, obtain a follow-up inspection, and submit an approved corrective action plan; if imported food labels are not Korean-compliant, replace labels under MFDS product registration procedure and re-apply for the food business report.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: District Gu Office Business and Health Division; Ministry of Food and Drug Safety; National Fire Agency; and local municipal building authority for structural and occupancy clearance
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Food Sales Business Report (General Food Retail Business) under the Food Sanitation Act; Business Registration Certificate under the Value-Added Tax Act; Fire Fighting Facilities Completion Certificate and Fire Safety Inspection Certificate under the Fire Facilities Installation and Maintenance Act

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Ministry of Environment (Metropolitan/Provincial Environmental Agency and local Gu Office)
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Environmental Registration / Small-Scale Environmental Review; full Environmental Impact Assessment is not required for a grocery store with total floor area below 10,000 square meters, provided the site is not in an environment-sensitive zone such as a greenbelt, watershed protection area, or natural park buffer; where the site is within a sensitive zone, a simplified environmental review must be registered before building occupancy.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: No industrial point-source discharge permit is required for routine grocery retail; sanitary sewage must connect to the municipal sewer network, and any on-site wastewater treatment effluent must comply with BOD 10 mg/L, COD 40 mg/L, TSS 40 mg/L, and pH 6.8-7.5 under the Water Environment Conservation Act; commercial refrigeration systems using controlled refrigerants must not emit more than 5 kilograms per year of ozone-depleting substances or fluorinated greenhouse gases; hazardous waste, including waste oil, fluorescent lamps, batteries, and contaminated containers, must be stored separately and disposed of by licensed collectors; if the store generates more than 500 kilograms per month of non-hazardous waste, it must submit a quarterly waste treatment report to the local Gu office.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: The premises must obtain a Certificate of Completion of Fire-Fighting Systems and a Fire Safety Inspection Certificate for commercial retail use, including verification of fire extinguishers, emergency exits, sprinkler controls, and evacuation signage; newly constructed or materially altered premises require a structural load and occupancy clearance from the municipal building authority; under the Occupational Safety and Health Act, a workplace with five or more employees must appoint a workplace safety and health manager, conduct initial and quarterly workplace hazard assessments, and post statutory safety notices, and the company must participate in local civil defense evacuation exercises if the building is classified as a multi-story public accommodation.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: National Tax Service (NTS) of the Republic of Korea; online electronic portal: HomeTax (Hometax) at www.hometax.go.kr; export and customs declarations are administered by the Korea Customs Service through its UNI-PASS electronic portal at unipass.customs.go.kr.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A foreign non-resident entity carrying on business in South Korea must apply for a ten-digit Business Registration Certificate (Sahop Deungnokjeung) within 20 days from commencing taxable business. The application is filed with the district tax office having jurisdiction over the domestic place of business, or, in the absence of a fixed place of business, with the director-designated tax office, and may be lodged through HomeTax or in person by a duly appointed domestic tax representative. The required documentation package includes the foreign company's certificate of incorporation or equivalent public registry extract, apostilled or consular-certified certificate of foreign registration, board resolution appointing the Korean in-country representative, written appointment of a tax representative for foreign non-resident taxpayers, evidence of the local business premises lease, passport copies of the controlling principals, and a power of attorney in favor of the domestic tax representative. Once NTS verifies the application, it issues the Business Registration Certificate, which simultaneously constitutes the Korean VAT registration, corporate income tax registration, and the statutory Tax Identification Number. The same registration number must be used on all VAT invoices, e-tax invoices, customs export declarations, and payroll withholding remittances; any material change in entity particulars must be reported to the district tax office within 15 days.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Entity_Level_Taxation: a Korean Yuhan Hoesa is mandatorily treated as a domestic corporation subject to Korean corporate income tax on its worldwide income, and the entity is the VAT taxpayer; there is no pass-through of income or tax attributes to shareholders under Korean domestic tax law.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: None applicable in the sense of a US-style check-the-box election or elective hybrid mismatch treatment. Korean tax law imposes entity-level taxation without elective pass-through. The only material election available is the domestic consolidated corporate income tax return regime under the Corporate Tax Act, which may be elected by a resident parent company and its 100% wholly-owned resident subsidiaries; group taxation is subject to strict continuing conditions. Foreign tax credit, branch profit election, and certain accounting-period/consolidation timing elections may apply under the corporate tax framework, but no hybrid mismatch election is available and anti-avoidance rules apply.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Value-Added Tax (VAT) under the Value-Added Tax Act of the Republic of Korea; there is no separate statewide or provincial sales tax in South Korea.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: Zero registration threshold: every person, including a foreign non-resident corporation, engaged in any taxable business in South Korea must register for VAT from business commencement regardless of turnover. A simplified VAT taxable person status is available for small business operators with annual taxable supplies not exceeding KRW 80,000,000, but such simplified taxpayers remain fully VAT-registered and must comply with e-tax invoice obligations.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Electronic tax invoices are mandatory for all VAT-registered entities in South Korea, including a Yuhan Hoesa engaged in grocery retail and export. The seller must issue a Korean-standard VAT tax invoice through HomeTax or an NTS-approved Electronic Tax Invoice service provider, and the electronic invoice data must be transmitted to the National Tax Service no later than the day following issuance. South Korea does not operate a real-time fiscal clearance or anti-fraud digital stamping model similar to Latin American regimes; instead, the NTS performs post-transaction cross-verification by matching e-tax invoice data, bank payment information, cash receipt data, customs export declarations, and foreign exchange receipt records. Issuance of false, inflated, or unregistered electronic tax invoices carries penalty taxes and may trigger criminal liability under the Punishment of Tax Evaders Act. For export supplies, the zero-rated export tax invoice must be retained together with the customs export declaration, transport documents, and proof of receipt of foreign currency.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Under Korean VAT law, goods exported outside South Korea are zero-rated, and certain services supplied to or used by a foreign non-resident outside Korea may also be zero-rated if the statutory conditions are satisfied. For the Asian supermarket grocery hub, zero-rating is available only where physical goods leave South Korea under customs export clearance, title and risk pass to an overseas non-resident buyer, the export transaction is supported by genuine commercial documentation, and foreign currency is received in respect of the export sale. Domestic retail sales in Korean premises remain taxable at 10% VAT.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (Bill of Entry) filed with Korea Customs Service through UNI-PASS and approved export clearance confirmation
Commercial invoice and packing list matching the export declaration and shipment details
Sales contract, purchase order, or equivalent binding evidence of the overseas transaction
Bill of Lading for sea freight or House/Master Air Waybill for air freight evidencing physical export movement from South Korea
Certificate of origin or export food-safety/phytosanitary certificate where required by the destination jurisdiction
Inward Remittance Certificate (FIRC) issued by the handling foreign exchange bank
Foreign currency bank credit advice or statement evidencing receipt and repatriation of export proceeds
Zero-rated VAT export tax invoice issued to the overseas buyer
Proof of the overseas buyer's non-resident status, such as the buyer's foreign business registration certificate or equivalent official identifier
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: The National Tax Service may audit export substantiation within the statutory tax assessment period, with longer periods for fraudulent underreporting. If zero-rated export treatment is not fully substantiated by customs evidence, transport documents, and foreign currency receipt records, or if the claimed export is found to be false, the NTS will claw back the 0% rate and assess VAT at 10% on the gross export supply value, together with past-due interest and statutory penalty taxes. Penalty taxes may include additional tax for unregistered turnover, false or unfiled tax invoices, underreported export sales, and improper electronic tax invoices; those penalties can be substantial and may exceed the underlying VAT. Criminal prosecution under the Punishment of Tax Evaders Act and the Korea Customs Service's customs violation proceedings can result in monetary fines, imprisonment, confiscation of the export proceeds, and permanent loss of zero-rating eligibility. Exporters must therefore retain the complete documentation bundle for at least the statutory record-keeping period and ensure that export proceeds are repatriated within 180 days, subject to the extension procedures established under Korean foreign exchange and customs administration.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Bank of Korea (BOK), acting with the Ministry of Economy and Finance (MOEF) as the responsible monetary and foreign exchange policy agency under the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act and the Foreign Exchange Information System (FEIS)
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: South Korea maintains a predominantly liberal current-account convertibility framework. Korean won (KRW) is freely convertible for trade settlements, service payments, and routine business expenses, subject to the repository reporting obligations of residents through authorized foreign exchange banks. Capital-account transactions are more administratively controlled: foreign direct investment inflows require filing under the Foreign Investment Promotion Act with KOTRA or a designated foreign exchange bank, and the remitted funds must be credited to a Foreign Investment Capital Account before being converted into KRW for business use. The surrender requirement for export proceeds has been substantively abolished, so exporters may retain foreign currency in domestic foreign-currency accounts. However, profit remittance and dividend repatriation to non-resident shareholders require submission of audited financial statements, tax clearance certificates, and bank verification of the capital verification certificate, and the bank is required to report the remittance to the BOK via FEIS. In practical underwriting terms, the regime is transparent and predictable for a low-risk grocery importer, but any mismatch between the stated investment purpose codes, capital account movement, and actual trade invoices will trigger automatic bank compliance review.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: There is no mandatory conversion ratio for export foreign currency receipts under South Korean law; the statutory surrender proportion is effectively 0%. Exporters must nonetheless receive export proceeds within a general statutory timeline of six months from the date of export declaration or the date the export goods are shipped, as specified under the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act and related Presidential Decrees. Proceeds must be received through an authorized foreign exchange bank and may be held in a domestic foreign-currency deposit account. If the six-month collection deadline is not met, the exporter must submit an extension application or report explaining the non-collection to the relevant authority through the foreign exchange bank. The bank is obligated to record the receipt, verify the underlying export customs declaration, and transmit the transaction data to the Foreign Exchange Information System (FEIS) within the data submission windows established by the BOK.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Foreign Investment Capital Account (KRW escrow and capital verification) plus Basic Operational Domestic Currency Account
Foreign Investment Capital Account plus Basic Operational KRW Account with multi-currency sub-ledger
Foreign Investment Capital Account plus Business Current Account with FX trading facility
Foreign Investment Capital Account plus Operational KRW Account and Trade Settlement Account
Basic Operational Current Account, retail-centric grocery settlement account, lower priority for FDI capital escrow

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: The viability of offshore fintech EMIs is low for the Korean entity. Fintech EMIs are not licensed as banks or foreign exchange banking institutions under the Korean Banking Act and Foreign Exchange Transactions Act, and they are legally barred from issuing domestic KRW account numbers, acting as settlement institutions for Korean tax payments, customs duties, utilities, or local POS/credit card merchant acquiring workflows. A foreign EMI could theoretically support a pre-funded multi-currency card for travel or minor expenses, but it cannot satisfy the statutory corporate banking requirements, foreign investment capital account opening, KRW clearing, or customs and tax settlement rails. The Korean subsidiary should use Tier-1 domestic commercial banks for all primary treasury functions and may use EMIs only as a supplementary procurement card for non-regulated cross-border purchases, never as a primary settlement rail.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Statutory directors who are responsible for the Korean entity are generally required to appear physically at the chosen commercial bank branch for the initial corporate account opening and KYC interview. A purely remote consular proxy opening is not accepted for full corporate banking privileges, online banking certificates, and foreign investment capital account creation. The representative director may nominate a local director with a valid Alien Registration Card (ARC) or a Korean resident director to serve as the signatory, but the ultimate foreign owner and statutory representative must still satisfy the bank through a physical interview, passport presentation, apostilled company documents, and execution of the corporate mandate. For subsequent transactions, account operation may be conducted through the bank's digital certificates after the in-branch enrollment is complete.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Opacity in the upstream beneficial ownership chain where the Korean LLC is owned by an Asian family trust or a chain of overseas investment vehicles
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Apostilled certificate of incorporation, full share register identifying every beneficial owner above 10%, notarized trust deed or holding-company declaration, source-of-wealth statement, passport copies of all UBOs, foreign bank reference letters, and a corporate organizational chart certified by the legal representative.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Unclear source of initial foreign investment capital and inability to distinguish the Korean capital verification deposit from operating cash flows
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Foreign investment certificate issued under the Foreign Investment Promotion Act, SWIFT MT103 credit confirmation with exact FDI purpose code, bank statement of the remitting entity proving legitimate source of funds, capital verification report from a licensed Korean public accountant, and a signed board resolution confirming the purpose of the capital injection.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Mismatch between the registered business address, the director's residential registration, and the actual grocery retail location used for customs and liquor/import licensing
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Valid lease agreement registered with the local district office, recent utility bill in the company name, business license (sae-upjajing) with corresponding business address, customs import license and health/food safety licensing documents, and a copy of the director's ARC or domestic residence certificate confirming physical presence.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Trade-related red flag where the Korean importer receives repetitive overseas remittances from related suppliers in a high-risk jurisdiction before customs clearing is complete
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Complete import purchase agreements, proforma invoices and commercial invoices, original bills of lading, customs import declarations and tax invoices, warehouse inventory photographs, product recall insurance documentation, supplier business registration copies, and three months of bank statements demonstrating that the remittance amounts correspond to actual trade obligations.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: The Korean LLC should submit a foreign investment report to KOTRA or a licensed foreign exchange bank before inward remittance. The injecting offshore parent then sends a SWIFT MT103 in USD, EUR, or KRW with the correct FDI purpose code, clearly referencing the Foreign Investment Certificate number. Funds are credited to the Foreign Investment Capital Account at the chosen Tier-1 bank, after which they can be converted into KRW at the market exchange rate and transferred into the operational current account. The bank will issue a capital verification certificate confirming the actual receipt of foreign currency and the KRW conversion. No corporate funds may be used for operations before the foreign investment report and capital verification are completed. All contingent liabilities and directors' loans must be separately declared; inbound remittances lacking the correct FDI code will be rejected by the bank's Foreign Exchange Information System checks.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Outbound settlement for imported Asian condiments and grocery products should be executed through ordinary bank transfers using SWIFT MT103 for open-account trade, documentary collections for smaller or first-time supplier relationships, and import letters of credit under UCP600 for larger volume procurement cycles. Payments denominated in USD, EUR, CNY, or KRW are acceptable if the underlying trade invoice and customs declarations are presented to the remitting bank. For Chinese supplier payments, a participating Korean bank can use CNH clearing via its RMB clearing arrangement or a separate CNH SWIFT line. All trade payments require the company to submit the import customs declaration, tax invoice, and supporting commercial document set to the bank so the payment can be accurately filed in FEIS. The grocery retail entity should maintain a small treasury buffer in KRW for payroll and fixed local costs, and a separate USD/CNH account for supplier settlements to reduce FX frequency and associated costs.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Onshore KRW/USD forward contracts executed with a Tier-1 Korean commercial bank under the real demand and underlying trade exposure principle
KRW/CNY and KRW/EUR forward contracts with underlying import payables and settled through the bank's domestic foreign exchange desk
Currency interest rate swaps and plain-vanilla FX options are permissible only where the notional matches the verified import purchase orders or export receivables

Offshore non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) are practically restricted for this Korean domestic entity; non-resident counterparties may trade NDFs outside Korea, but the Korean bank is generally prohibited from settling KRW NDFs for the local LLC without express regulatory permission, so such instruments are not recommended

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual General Meeting of Members and Approval of Financial Statements
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Company's shareholder body (documented in the minutes; any newly appointed directors must be registered with the Commercial Registry of the Supreme Court of Korea)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: By March 31 for a calendar-year company (within three months after fiscal year-end); newly appointed directors must be registered within 30 days of appointment
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to convene the AGM or to register director changes within 30 days triggers administrative fines up to KRW 2,000,000 per violation and may result in judicial compulsion; persistent non-compliance can lead to a court order for the dissolution of the company

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Corporate Income Tax Return and Payment
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: National Tax Service of the Republic of Korea (NTS)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: March 31 following the taxable year for a December 31 year-end company; automatically extended to May 31 if the return is prepared and signed by an accredited tax agent (tax accountant or CPA)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Non-filing penalty: 20% of the corporate tax amount; misstatement/understatement: 10%-40% negligence penalties; late payment interest: 0.022% per day on unpaid tax (about 8.03% per annum); failure to file for three consecutive years authorizes NTS to demand compulsory liquidation or administrative strike-off through the court

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Local Income Tax Surtax on Corporate Tax
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Local Government / City or Provincial Revenue Office
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within one month after the corresponding corporate income tax return deadline (generally by April 30; extendable to June 30 if the corporate tax deadline is extended)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Surcharge of 0.3% per day on unpaid local income tax (subject to a statutory cap); penalties parallel to corporate tax deficiencies; continuous default leads to coercive collection and potential registration suspension

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Semi-annual Value Added Tax Return and Payment - First Half (January-June)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: July 25 of the same fiscal year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing penalty: 10% of unpaid VAT; additional daily overdue charge may apply; failure to pay for two consecutive periods can trigger seizure of assets and mandatory deregistration

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Semi-annual Value Added Tax Return and Payment - Second Half (July-December)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: January 25 of the following fiscal year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing penalty: 10% of unpaid VAT; additional daily overdue charge may apply; failure to pay for two consecutive periods can trigger seizure of assets and mandatory deregistration

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Yearly Employer's Withholding and Wage Deduction Statement (Payroll Return)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: February 10 of the following year for all salary and wage payments made in the prior calendar year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to file the withholding statement: penalty equal to 1% of the unreported amounts (plus further penalties for foreign employees); repeated non-compliance can be treated as tax evasion, leading to criminal fines and/or administrative strike-off

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Under the Korean Act on External Audit of Stock Companies (as applied to all companies including a Yuhan Hoesa), an independent certified public accountant must be engaged for the annual statutory audit if, based on the preceding fiscal year-end financial statements, the company records total assets of KRW 12 billion or more (approximately USD 9.2 million). The Financial Services Commission may also mandate an audit for listed entities, public-interest companies, or entities designated by administrative order; a company with an average headcount of 300 or more employees is also commonly designated for audit. Annual gross turnover of KRW 10 billion (approximately USD 7.7 million) is an additional indication that a precautionary audit review should be commissioned, although the primary statutory trigger remains the asset-based threshold.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Korea implements International Financial Reporting Standards as K-IFRS for listed entities and financial institutions. Private limited companies (Yuhan Hoesa) may apply K-GAAP (General Corporate Accounting Standards, Korean SME GAAP) or K-IFRS. The statutory audit, if applicable, must be conducted in accordance with Korean Standards on Auditing (KSA), which are aligned with International Standards on Auditing (ISA).

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: South Korea does not maintain a public annual UBO register. Instead, the company must (i) record all members and transfer activities in the statutory Register of Members; (ii) notify the Korean Commercial Registry (Supreme Court of Korea) of any share transfer, change of members, or change in ultimate beneficial ownership within 30 days of such event; and (iii) internally confirm and document the current beneficial ownership structure at least once per calendar year for anti-money laundering compliance with financial institutions and the Act on Reporting and Using Specific Financial Transaction Information. Failure to keep the register up to date is punishable by administrative fines and may invalidate certain resolutions.

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 350 - USD 1,200 per annum for a registered office or corporate agent service in South Korea (typically KRW 500,000 - KRW 1,800,000).
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 2,500 - USD 9,000 per annum for an independent statutory audit of a small-to-mid grocery retail entity under Korean GAAP (fees vary with asset size, transaction count and complexity).

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 24% national corporate income tax maximum bracket plus 10% local income tax surtax, producing a 26.4% composite headline rate; progressive brackets are 9% up to KRW 200 million, 19% above KRW 200 million and up to KRW 20 billion, 21% above KRW 20 billion and up to KRW 300 billion, and 24% above KRW 300 billion
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Statutory incentives include foreign investment tax holidays under Article 121 of the Foreign Investment Promotion Act for qualifying high-tech facilities, Free Economic Zone corporate income tax holiday programs for designated innovative business, SME tax deduction preferences, R&D tax credits, and foreign tax credit for foreign-source income; a specialty grocery importer-retailer will generally qualify only if located in a designated free economic zone and certified as a qualifying high-tech or support business

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Corporate Income Tax Standard Return Form (Form 1) and accompanying schedules filed electronically through the HomeTax national tax portal (hometax.go.kr)
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual; quarterly advance corporate income tax payments are required for corporations with prior-year tax liability exceeding KRW 500 million
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Within three months after the end of the fiscal year, i.e. by March 31 of the following year for calendar-year taxpayers; a one-month extension is available with NTS approval, and a further extension may apply for foreign corporations with overseas accounting records

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: All gross revenue from grocery retail sales, including imported Asian condiments, vegetables, packaged foods, and any incidental income, reported on the accrual basis before any deductions.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Report only Korean-source sales attributable to the domestic trade or business; exclude sales booked to a foreign head office unless a Korean permanent establishment exists; attach customs entry and e-tax invoice summaries; ensure intercompany procurement prices are at arm's length to avoid transfer pricing recharacterization.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 2 (Cost of Goods Sold and Operating Expenses)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Inventoried cost of imported and local goods, salaries, rent, utilities, logistics, depreciation, repairs, marketing, and insurance expenses incurred in the Korean retail operation.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Imported inventory costs must be substantiated by customs declarations, bills of lading, supplier invoices, and payment evidence; expenses paid to foreign related parties are deductible only when supported by transfer pricing documentation and when the corresponding withholding tax, if any, has been properly reported; disallowance arises for unsupported offshore management fees.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Income items exempted by domestic law or tax treaty, including certain dividend exclusion amounts, capital gains specifically exempted, and non-business subsidies meeting statutory exemption conditions.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A non-resident corporation with no Korean permanent establishment must list only Korean-source income that is exempted by an applicable double tax agreement; attach a tax residency certificate and treaty claim schedule when relying on DTA protection; otherwise all Korean-source income remains taxable.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Net income per the Korean GAAP or IFRS financial statements after matching revenue with cost of goods sold and operating expenses, before corporate tax adjustments.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Cross-border accruals must be reconciled with currency translation rules; no deduction is allowed for reserves or accruals that lack economic substance; align the book income with the arm's length results of the Korean retail entity.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Statutory adjustments adding back non-deductible expenses and deducting tax-allowed reserves, including entertainment expense overages, donation disallowances, depreciation differences, and bad debt reserve adjustments.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Any payment to a non-resident, such as notional royalties or commissions, that was not subject to proper domestic withholding may be treated as non-deductible; watch the thin capitalization and excessive interest expense disallowance under the International Tax Adjustment Act.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxable income for the year after applying loss carryforwards, tax adjustment additions, tax adjustment deductions, and non-taxable income exclusions.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: For a non-resident corporate taxpayer without a Korean permanent establishment, the tax base is limited to items enumerated in the Corporate Income Tax Act as Korean-source income; attach a sourcing schedule for each revenue stream and avoid using treaty shopping entities lacking economic substance.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 7 (Corporate Tax Rate and Calculated National Tax)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Application of the progressive corporate income tax brackets to the taxable income tax base and computation of national corporate income tax.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Compute tax at the progressive national rates and separately compute the 10% local income tax surtax; if a permanent establishment has treaty-protected income, carve those amounts out of the base and document the attribution of profits and expenses to the permanent establishment under the authorized OECD approach.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Statement of eligible tax credits such as foreign tax credit, investment tax credit, SME employment credit, research and development credit, and withholding tax credits.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Attach the foreign tax credit schedule in the foreign currency used by the foreign branch or payor; a non-resident corporate shareholder receiving Korean-source dividends cannot claim dividend-received deduction without treaty exposure; verify residency in the treaty jurisdiction before claiming credits.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Quarterly advance corporate income tax installments already paid, corporate tax withheld at source on interest or dividend income, and any provisional payments made during the fiscal year.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Reconcile advance payments with the HomeTax payment ledger; non-resident withholding agents should attach certificate of Korean tax withheld; overpayments are carried as refund credits only after the return is filed.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Final corporate tax liability after deducting advance payments and tax credits from the calculated tax, resulting in additional tax due or refund.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: If additional tax is due, remit by bank transfer on or before the statutory deadline to avoid daily late payment surcharge; if a claim for treaty-reduced rate results in over-withholding, the refund route is a separate corrected return or claim filed with NTS within three years; never net treaty benefit unilaterally without approved documentation.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late or non-filing carries a penalty of 20% of the final tax payable (40% where the failure is fraudulent); underreporting an amount not based on fraud carries 10% of the underpaid tax, rising to 40% where fraud is established; late payment accrues at 0.022% per day; false e-tax invoice issuance attracts 1% to 2% penalties on supply value; serious evasion triggers criminal prosecution under the Punishment of Tax Evasion Act with imprisonment up to three years and fines up to KRW 100 million.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 22% composite withholding tax on outbound dividends payable to non-resident shareholders: 20% national corporate income tax withholding plus 10% local income tax surtax on that withholding (20% x 1.10 = 22%).
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To claim reduced dividend, interest, or royalty withholding under a bilateral income tax treaty, the foreign beneficial owner must deliver to the Korean withholding agent before payment a treaty rate application statement, a valid Tax Residency Certificate issued by the foreign competent authority showing treaty residence, a beneficial ownership declaration and supporting corporate charters/ownership structure, and a statement that the income is not effectively connected with a Korean permanent establishment; the Korean payer must retain these documents and may be required to file them with the National Tax Service; if the full domestic rate was withheld, the foreign taxpayer may file a refund request with the NTS within three years, but a generally effective rate reduction requires the withholding agent mechanism to be used in the first instance.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Statutory domestic withholding on cross-border interest and royalties paid to non-residents is 22% composite (20% national withholding plus 2% local surtax); treaty rates vary by jurisdiction and typically reduce interest withholding to 10%-15% and royalties to 10%-15%, subject to beneficial ownership and absence of a Korean permanent establishment; royalties paid for the use of trademarks, copyrighted retail software, or patents in Korea remain subject to treaty relief only when the payee is the legal and beneficial owner in a treaty jurisdiction.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: KRW 10 billion aggregate cross-border related-party transactions in a fiscal year triggers the mandatory preparation and submission of Local File and Master File transfer pricing documentation to the Korean tax administration; lower documentation requirements may apply in tax audits, and contemporaneous TP documentation is required for transactions with specially related parties in low-tax jurisdictions
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Korea does not apply Gulf-style Economic Substance Regulations, but the National Tax Service enforces substance-over-form doctrines through the Corporate Income Tax Act and Article 12 of the International Tax Adjustment Act to deny DTA benefits where obtaining treaty benefits is the principal purpose; for permanent establishment attribution, the tax office requires Core Income-Generating Activities (CIGA) to be identified in Korea, and intercompany arrangements between the Korean retail entity and offshore purchasing entities must show real inventory, management, employees, and risk assumption in Korea.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: The Korean supermarket LLC suppresses cash and card sales at POS terminals, issues no e-tax invoices to local restaurant-chain buyers, inflates the cost of imported Asian condiments through a related Hong Kong supplier, and fabricates expense invoices to keep taxable income artificially under the KRW 200 million lower bracket.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Article 10 of the Punishment of Tax Evasion Act (jo-sae-beom cheob-ryeo-beop): imprisonment up to three years and/or a fine up to KRW 100 million; in addition, the NTS imposes national tax penalties of up to 40% of the evaded corporate income tax under the Framework Act on National Taxes, plus a 10% local surcharge and late payment surcharge of 0.022% per day.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors are jointly and severally liable for the corporate tax shortfall and penalties when corporate assets are insufficient, under Article 39 of the Framework Act on National Taxes; personal bank accounts, real estate, and vehicles may be seized; the NTS may impose a departure restriction/travel ban; if the evasion involves fraudulent acts, the director faces criminal imprisonment and disqualification from serving as a director or auditor.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Shell Company / Lack of Economic Substance and Treaty Abuse
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: The Korean Yuhan Hoesa is operated as a paper LLC with no physical grocery store, no employees, no board meetings in Korea, no inventory risk, and no logistics management; all retail margin is shifted to a related Hong Kong procurement company through unsubstantiated markups, and the non-resident equity holder claims treaty withholding exemption on dividends without any real activity in the residence country.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Article 5 of the International Tax Adjustment Act empowers the National Tax Service to re-determine income at arm's length and impose penalty taxes of 20% to 40% on the adjusted understatement; Article 12 denies double tax treaty relief where one of the principal purposes is treaty shopping; under the Commercial Act Articles 399 and 401, courts may pierce the corporate veil to hold directors jointly liable for damages caused by intentional or negligent abuse of the corporate form.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Each director becomes personally liable for the full recomputed tax, additional charges, and civil damages to the company and creditors; personal asset restitution is enforceable through NTS collection proceedings; the director is blacklisted as a delinquent taxpayer and subject to travel ban; if the shell was used to defraud creditors or tax authorities, criminal charges for fraud and aggravated tax evasion may lead to imprisonment for up to five years.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: AML, E-Tax Invoice Fraud, and Foreign Exchange Violations
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: The retailer fails to register and issue electronic tax invoices for B2B sales to Korean restaurant chains, routes cash grocery receipts through personal bank accounts of directors to avoid reporting, and repatriates profits as undocumented management fees or hidden payments to a foreign related company without declaring the transactions under the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: The VAT Act imposes penalties of up to 2% of the supply value for each unissued e-tax invoice; the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act imposes administrative fines and criminal penalties for unregistered outbound payment transactions; the Financial Transaction Reports Act imposes fines for failure to report suspicious transactions; the tax administration also disallows the related expense deductions and imposes additional corporate income tax penalties.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors are secondarily liable under the Framework Act on National Taxes for unpaid VAT and corporate income tax; personal assets can be restrained and a travel ban imposed for tax delinquencies; the use of personal bank accounts for business revenue may trigger embezzlement charges against the director; criminal conviction may result in imprisonment up to three years under the Punishment of Tax Evasion Act and additional liability under the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act for unlicensed capital movements.
